presentation.summary: Erect a scaffold beside an overhead power line while controlling electrical clearance, foundation stability, long materials and an arcing event.
presentation.role: You are the safety professional coordinating scaffold erection near an overhead electrical line.
presentation.situation: A scaffold must be erected close to an overhead line. Voltage uncertainty, long conductive components, ground conditions and wind create interacting electrical and scaffold risks.
presentation.objective: Maintain verified electrical separation and scaffold integrity, and prevent approach after any electrical contact until the supply is made safe.
knownFacts: The line voltage is initially unconfirmed.
Long metal standards and tubes will be handled.
The scaffold base includes compacted fill.
Wind can move long conductive components toward the line.

contact_decision_defensible.observable: The immediate area is secured and help is mobilized, but one element of the respond to electrical contact response remains less complete than the preferred plan.
contact_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: This action can reduce harm, but the BEST response integrates personnel protection, alarm, isolation and planned emergency control without leaving a material response gap.

contact_decision_weak.observable: Some protective action is taken, but personnel remain closer to the hazard than necessary during the respond to electrical contact response. The margin for a secondary casualty narrows.
contact_decision_weak.guidedInsight: A partial emergency action may sound practical, but it is weak when it keeps people exposed or delays full hazard-zone control.

contact_decision_best.observable: The team activates the planned emergency response at the respond to electrical contact stage, keeps people out of the hazard zone and controls the event before re-entry.
contact_decision_best.guidedInsight: The strongest emergency choice protects responders first. Rescue, isolation and source control should follow the planned capability rather than expose another person.

contact_decision_critical.observable: An unprotected or inadequately controlled intervention is attempted during the respond to electrical contact stage. The event escalates and a secondary casualty or larger release becomes credible.
contact_decision_critical.guidedInsight: Critical emergency decisions often fail by sending people toward an uncontrolled hazard. Protect responders and establish control before attempting intervention.

closeout_decision_defensible.observable: The team strengthens the immediate controls and uses a controlled restart review, but the closeout does not explore the underlying failure as completely as the BEST path.
closeout_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: Corrective action is valuable, but restart assurance is stronger when the underlying cause and all affected safeguards are verified.

closeout_decision_weak.observable: The team corrects the most visible problem and prepares to resume the scaffold-erection task before the full causal chain has been resolved.
closeout_decision_weak.guidedInsight: A technically acceptable local fix can still be weak if it restores production before learning and system-level corrections are complete.

closeout_decision_critical.observable: The scaffold-erection task is pushed toward restart after only superficial recovery. Critical causes or damaged safeguards remain unresolved.
closeout_decision_critical.guidedInsight: Restart pressure can recreate the same hazard. A major event is more likely when work resumes before critical barriers are restored and verified.

closeout_decision_best.observable: The scaffold-erection task remains suspended while causes, damaged safeguards and corrective actions are verified. Work is reauthorized only after a safe basis is re-established.
closeout_decision_best.guidedInsight: Safe closeout is not simply returning conditions to normal. It must address why control was lost and verify the barriers needed for a safe restart.

safe_completion.title: Safe completion
safe_completion.narrative: The scaffold-erection task was completed with the critical hazards controlled and changing conditions managed before escalation.
safe_completion.keyTurningPoint: You maintained verified electrical clearance and scaffold stability before handling conductive components.

controlled_recovery.title: Controlled recovery
controlled_recovery.narrative: The scaffold-erection task developed a significant control weakness, but later decisions restored a controlled state before serious harm occurred.
controlled_recovery.keyTurningPoint: A clearance or erection control weakened, but work was stopped and the safe method was restored.

incident_contained.title: Incident contained
incident_contained.narrative: The scenario developed into an incident, but emergency and recovery actions contained the event and limited its consequences.
incident_contained.keyTurningPoint: An electrical-contact event occurred, but separation and supply isolation prevented further exposure.

major_incident.title: Major incident
major_incident.narrative: Unresolved control failures allowed the scaffold-erection task to escalate into a major incident requiring extended response, investigation and corrective action.
major_incident.keyTurningPoint: Electrical and scaffold-control weaknesses combined into a major worksite incident.

critical_failure.title: Critical failure
critical_failure.narrative: The decision path produced a severe uncontrolled outcome in the scaffold-erection task. Recovery options were overwhelmed by a critical barrier failure.
critical_failure.keyTurningPoint: A critical electrical-separation rule was bypassed when conductive material approached the energized line.
